answers.trace:
WHAT THE SOFTWARE DOES, END TO END — traced from the code on 2026-08-23. The human steps around it are NOT in the repo and are the meeting's job.

SETUP (per client workspace, in this order — the Overview enforces it as a numbered 1-7 workflow)
1. Create the workspace. It starts in Onboarding.
2. Brief — identity, ICP, positioning, compliance.
3. Mailboxes — connect the CLIENT'S OWN Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace mailbox by OAuth. This is the whole architecture: we send AS them, from their domain, so SPF/DKIM/DMARC already pass and the client changes no DNS.
4. Sources — contacts arrive by CSV import or RocketReach enrichment. They land in the cross-client ContactUniverse warehouse first, then get attached to a client list.
5. Do-not-contact — connect the client's Google Sheet of blocked addresses/domains.
6. Templates, then a sequence built from them, then approve it.
7. Review recipients, then Launch.

A SEND (sendSequenceStepBatch, src/server/email-sequences/send-introduction.ts)
- Loads sequence, step and template scoped by clientId at every hop, and refuses if any of them belongs to a different client.
- Resolves the opt-out rail: a hosted unsubscribe link ONLY on the client's own aligned link domain (go.<their-domain>); with none configured it falls back to a mailto: opt-out on the sending mailbox, so the email carries no host but the sender's own.
- Per recipient: suppression/DNC check, send-governance decision, 10-day cooldown, then reserve a slot against that mailbox's daily cap and its warm-up ramp (starts at 5/day, +5 every 5 days by mailbox age).
- Writes an OutboundEmail row as QUEUED. Nothing has left yet.

DISPATCH (GitHub Actions, every 5 minutes, 07:00-18:00 UK, weekdays only)
- Re-checks suppression and hard bounces at dispatch time — not just at queue time.
- Sends through the connected mailbox via Graph or Gmail. There is NO ESP fallback: if the mailbox cannot send, the row fails rather than silently rerouting.
- Stamps our own Message-ID so genuine replies can be linked back, and records providerMessageId + sentAt. That pair is what the product calls "send proof".

REPLIES (GitHub Actions, every 15 minutes, same window)
- Pulls the mailbox inbox. Detects NDR/DSN bounce-backs first (that is the only bounce signal — Graph and Gmail give no delivery webhook) and suppresses the failed address.
- Filters out internal staff mail, stores the raw message, then matches a reply to an outbound three ways: our stamped Message-ID, thread references, or contact-email fallback. No reply row is created unless a matching outbound exists IN THAT CLIENT.
- A matched reply stops the remaining follow-ups, and an opt-out-shaped reply suppresses the address for future campaigns too.

ASK IN THE MEETING — the parts no repository can answer:
- Where do the lists actually come from before the CSV? Who builds them, in what, and who checks them?
- Who writes the copy, and who signs it off before Launch is pressed?
- What happens between a reply landing and a meeting being booked? Is that in ODoutreach at all, or in someone's inbox?
- Which of the seven setup steps do they actually find hard?
answers.who:
THE PERMISSION MODEL AS ENFORCED IN CODE, verified live 2026-08-23. Note this is a SINGLE-COMPANY INTERNAL TOOL, not a customer-facing SaaS.

WHO CAN GET IN AT ALL
- Sign-in is Microsoft Entra ID. An identity with no matching StaffUser row is refused — the app never creates accounts. Optional STAFF_EMAIL_DOMAINS narrows it further.
- StaffUser.isActive is the on/off switch.

ANY ACTIVE STAFF MEMBER — and this is the important one
- Sees and works in EVERY live client workspace. getAccessibleClientIds (src/server/tenant/access.ts) does not consult membership at all.
- Can create clients, import contacts, connect mailboxes, edit templates, build and launch sequences, read all activity and replies, manage do-not-contact.
- In-account roles were REMOVED in 2026-06. The role column still exists but no read path uses it.
- This is deliberate: OpensDoors is an agency and its staff run outreach across all of its customers. Recorded as a decision in specs/BC-01-tenant-isolation.md with the three triggers that reverse it.

SUPER-ADMIN ONLY (StaffUser.isSuperAdmin — currently Greg)
- Soft-delete, restore and hard-purge a whole workspace.
- The deleted-workspaces page, staff invite/access controls, mailbox connection diagnostics, the /operations/outbound queue tools, and the RocketReach debug JSON.

NOBODY
- Clients themselves have no login. There is no customer-facing account of any kind.

DORMANT
- ClientMembership rows can be created and are stored, but no read path consults them. If a staff member ever needs scoping to one client, that table is the mechanism and it already exists.

ASK IN THE MEETING:
- Who at OpensDoors actually holds an account today, and should any of them NOT see every client?
- Will a client ever be given a login to see their own results? That is a different product if yes.
- Is there a contractor or freelancer case coming? That is trigger #2 for reversing the access decision.
answers.things:
WHAT THE SYSTEM HOLDS, AND HOW EACH ONE ENDS — read from prisma/schema.prisma on 2026-08-23. The honest headline: ONLY ONE THING HAS AN ENDING.

Client (a customer workspace) — ENDS properly. Super-admin soft-deletes it (deletedAt stamped, it disappears from every normal path), then a separate explicit hard purge. That purge is the ONLY deletion event in the system.

Everything below ends ONLY when its Client is purged, by database cascade. None has a lifetime of its own, no retention period, and no scheduled cleanup exists anywhere:
- Contact — a prospect. Name, email, phone, LinkedIn, employer, title, location.
- ContactList — an import batch turned into a sendable list.
- OutboundEmail — every email sent, INCLUDING the full body snapshot.
- InboundReply and InboundMailboxMessage — replies and raw synced mail, including full body text.
- ClientEmailSequence / enrollments — sequences can be ARCHIVED, which stops them sending but deletes nothing.
- ClientMailboxIdentity — a connected mailbox and its OAuth tokens.
- UnsubscribeToken — marked usedAt when redeemed, never removed.

TWO THINGS DO NOT END AT ALL, and both matter:
1. ContactUniverse — the cross-client prospect warehouse. It has NO clientId and is deduplicated across every client. Purging a workspace does NOT remove it. A prospect's name, email, phone and LinkedIn survive the deletion of the only client that ever knew them.
2. SuppressedEmail / SuppressedDomain — a record that a named person asked never to be contacted. This one SHOULD outlive everything, or deleting a contact silently un-suppresses them. But note the asymmetry found this weekend: bounce and unsubscribe suppressions are append-only, while Google-Sheet-sourced suppression is REPLACE-ON-SYNC — remove a row from the client's sheet and that address becomes sendable again.

So: there is no retention policy in code, and "deleted" currently means "hidden from staff", not erased. Under UK GDPR storage limitation that is a real gap, and it is recorded in .bidlow/CLASSIFY.json under regulated_data.

ASK IN THE MEETING:
- When a client leaves, what has OpensDoors promised happens to their prospect data — and by when?
- Does that promise appear in any contract already signed?
- Should a prospect deleted from a client still remain in the shared Universe for other clients to use? (Commercially useful, and the sharpest privacy question in the product.)
answers.exceptions:
WHEN IT LAST WENT WRONG — a real register, all found and evidenced between 2026-08-09 and 2026-08-23. Not hypothetical edge cases.

1. THE QUARANTINE — the big one. Every outreach email carried an unsubscribe link on opensdoors.bidlow.co.uk while the From: address was the customer's own domain. That mismatch is the textbook phishing signal and it got mail quarantined. It was NOT an authentication failure — SPF/DKIM/DMARC were passing all along. Fixed and tested 2026-08-22 (branch feat/zero-dns-send-profile); the app-domain fallback was removed entirely so it cannot return by accident.

2. DO-NOT-CONTACT MISSED SUBDOMAINS. Suppressing bt.com did not stop a send to someone@newsletter.bt.com — the lookup was an exact match. Fixed 2026-08-22, matching now walks up the domain's parents on label boundaries (so notbt.com and bt.com.evil.net still correctly do NOT match).

3. A PROSPECT ROW WITH NO MAILBOX WOULD HAVE BEEN SILENTLY MOCK-"SENT". The dispatcher routed on whether a mailbox was attached; rows without one fell through to a mock provider that returns success. In production that means an email recorded as sent that never existed. Fixed 2026-08-09.

4. STAFF ISOLATION WAS ASSERTED, THEN FOUND ABSENT. A test claimed a staff member could not see another client's data. Run for the first time on 2026-08-22, it failed: any active staff member can open every workspace. This turned out to be the intended agency design, not a defect — but nobody had written that down, so a test spent nine days asserting the opposite.

5. THE PRODUCT CONTRADICTS ITSELF ABOUT ITS OWN SENDS. A client's Overview reads "Activity — not started" while that same client's Activity tab reads "EMAILS SENT 1". Two different sources of truth. Reproduced 2026-08-23. Not yet fixed.

6. E-06 — ONE MAILBOX ON TWO WORKSPACES DUPLICATES INBOUND MAIL. The same address may be connected to two clients; each then stores its own copy of every raw inbound message, body text included. Replies do not cross; the raw store does. Found 2026-08-23, not fixed.

7. THE BOUNCE NUMBER READS ZERO AND NOBODY KNOWS WHY. Detection is switched ON in production, yet 0% across 1,209 sends. Either genuinely clean or silently not matching. Unresolved.

ASK IN THE MEETING:
- What went wrong from OPENSDOORS' side — a client complaint, a prospect who reacted badly, a list that turned out wrong? None of that is in the repo.
- What did they have to do by hand to recover, and how long did it take?

NEW CLIENT WORKSPACES: 1-5 a month.

CLIENTS LEAVING: 1-2 a month. On leaving, the customer's details are kept in a MANUAL FOLDER and are not tracked by the system. Offboarding is entirely outside the product.

ANGRY REPLIES / REMOVAL REQUESTS OUTSIDE THE UNSUBSCRIBE LINK: NOT OBSERVED.
CORRECTED BY GREG 2026-08-24. His words: "we have not received responses with do
not contact me, we have had unsubscribe links clicked, but no one responding, take
me off the list." The previous entry here said DAILY. That figure was drafted by
the agent and never checked with him, and finding F-01 was raised HIGH on the

to be removed.

MAILBOX DISCONNECTS: Greg does not know how often, and does not know who notices. Recorded as an unknown, not as zero.

UPDATED DO-NOT-CONTACT SHEETS FROM CLIENTS: weekly for some customers, monthly for others.

answers.not_handling:
DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE — decisions on record, so neither side assumes the other thought about it.

1. NO ISOLATION BETWEEN STAFF. Every active staff member sees every client workspace. This is the agency model and it is intentional. It reverses the day (a) a second agency shares the instance, (b) a staff member must be scoped to one client — a contractor or a client-side user, or (c) a client contractually requires named individuals only. ClientMembership already exists, inert, as the mechanism. SELLING A SHARED INSTANCE TO TWO AGENCIES WHO MUST NOT SEE EACH OTHER IS A REBUILD, NOT A FEATURE.

2. NO DELIVERY WEBHOOKS. Because we send through the client's own mailbox rather than a bulk ESP, no provider tells us an email was delivered. "Delivered" is shown as "Not tracked" rather than guessed. Bounces are detected only from NDR/DSN bounce-backs arriving in the mailbox.

3. RELATED COMPANY DOMAINS ARE NOT SUPPRESSED. Do-not-contact for bt.com does not cover bteurope.com. This cannot be derived from a string, so it is a client business rule and needs an explicit per-client list. Awaiting Greg's decision.

4. NO SEPARATE SENDING SUBDOMAIN AND NO TRACKING DOMAIN. Sending is from the client's existing mailbox on their ROOT domain — that is what makes the zero-DNS architecture work, and the trade is that the client's ordinary business domain carries the reputation risk. Open tracking is currently switched OFF entirely in production.

5. NO CORPORATE-VS-SOLE-TRADER DISTINCTION AT IMPORT. UK PECR turns on the recipient's legal structure — limited companies need no prior consent, sole traders do. The import pipeline cannot tell them apart, so that question cannot currently be answered per recipient. Named in DOMAIN-BRIEF-cold-email.md as a genuine, billable product gap.

6. NO RETENTION OR ERASURE. Nothing deletes prospect data on age; there is no scheduled cleanup and no erasure-on-request path.

7. NO AUTOMATIC STOP ON A BAD CAMPAIGN. Bounce rate is displayed but no send path reads it. A list bouncing at 30% is stopped only by a person noticing. This is why the pilot runs at a hard 20/day cap.

ASK IN THE MEETING:
- Which of these is OpensDoors already telling clients the product DOES do? That mismatch is the one that becomes a complaint.
answers.unknowns:
WHAT WE GENUINELY DO NOT KNOW YET — recorded 2026-08-23. Cheap now, expensive at launch.

1. [RESOLVED 2026-08-23 — see DOMAIN.json diagnoses/BOUNCE-0PCT] WHY THE BOUNCE RATE READS 0% ACROSS 1,209 SENDS. ANSWER: the NDR path suppresses the address but never sets OutboundEmail.status=BOUNCED, and that status is exactly what the report counts. Detection works; the measurement was wired to a column nothing on the live path writes. Remaining unknown is only HOW MANY NDRs have actually arrived, which needs the production database. ORIGINAL NOTE FOLLOWS: MAILBOX_BOUNCE_DETECTION_ENABLED is true in production and the NDR/DSN path is built and wired in. So something switched on is reporting nothing. Either delivery really is that clean, or the matcher is not linking bounce-backs to the rows that caused them. Until this is settled, the one threshold the domain brief calls non-negotiable (bounce rate under 2%) cannot be enforced — which is exactly why the pilot cap exists.

2. WHETHER "SEND PROOF MISSING" IS ENTIRELY A MEASUREMENT BUG. 204 of ~1,470 contacts show it. It is not a flag — it is an arithmetic difference between two tables, and seedExclusion is applied to one side and not the other, so every internal seed send inflates it by one. That explains SOME of it. Nobody has confirmed it explains ALL of it.

3. WHETHER /operations STILL 404s IN PRODUCTION. It returned 404 on 2026-08-09. On the branch build it 404s because there is no /operations/page.tsx at all — it is a route segment, not a page, and nothing links to it. Probably a non-issue, but it has not been re-checked live.

4. WHETHER THE CAMPAIGNS COLUMN IS WRONG AT SCALE. It read 0 for all 17 clients on production, including ones with hundreds of contacts. Could not be confirmed or refuted on a fixture database.

5. ART.28 DPAs WITH SENTRY, ROCKETREACH AND RESEND ARE NOT IN PLACE. Microsoft and Google are covered by their standard terms. These three are an open legal obligation, outstanding NOW rather than at some later milestone.

6. ROCKETREACH'S LAWFUL BASIS. Separate from the DPA and sharper: on what basis was the prospect data we BUY collected, and can that basis be relied on downstream? This is a controller question, not a processor one.

7. WHETHER ANY REAL SEND STILL WORKS END TO END ON THE CURRENT BUILD. Nobody has driven compose to send to reply since the changes. Deliberate — no live sends during development — but it means the core journey is unproven rather than proven working.

new_requirements.what: Remove Google Sheets as the list-import route. Accept CSV imports instead.
new_requirements.note: Google Sheets is currently BOTH the prospect-list route and the suppression-sync route. Removing it touches suppression as well as import — check the blast radius before scoping.

new_requirements.what: On import, the system must look for DUPLICATES.
new_requirements.note: Duplicate within one client, or across all clients? A prospect legitimately appearing on two different clients' lists is not the same thing as a duplicate within one. Needs settling before build.

new_requirements.what: On import, current do-not-contact contacts must not be removed.
new_requirements.note: This is the business-side statement of a defect already found in the code: sheet-sourced suppression is REPLACE-ON-SYNC — deleteMany then rewrite — so removing a row from a client sheet makes that address sendable again. Greg reached the same conclusion from operations without seeing the code.

findings_from_stage_1.what: Removal requests arriving OUTSIDE the unsubscribe link have NOT been observed. Recipients click the unsubscribe link; nobody replies asking to be taken off the list.
findings_from_stage_1.correction_quote: we have not received responses with do not contact me, we have had unsubscribe links clicked, but no one responding, take me off the list.
findings_from_stage_1.what_was_claimed: Removal requests arriving outside the unsubscribe link happen DAILY and are handled by hand.
findings_from_stage_1.why_it_was_wrong: The DAILY figure was drafted into the artefact and never checked against what OpensDoors had actually seen. It was not something Greg said; it was inferred and then written down as fact. Once written it read as evidence, and the HIGH severity, the 'daily exception is a FEATURE' conclusion and the compliance-exposure framing were all built on top of it.
findings_from_stage_1.why_not_deleted: The finding is downgraded, not removed. The underlying obligation is real and unchanged: an opt-out is legally an opt-out however it arrives, and the reply-ingest path must keep classifying opt-out language in a reply body. What changed is the FREQUENCY, and therefore the priority - this is a correctness requirement to maintain, not a daily manual workload to automate away.
findings_from_stage_1.why: Kept as a LOW standing requirement: opt-out language in a reply must continue to be detected and suppressed, because the day it does arrive it is a legal obligation. It is no longer evidence of a daily manual burden.
findings_from_stage_1.related: The 2026-08-24 fix to opt-out body starvation (PR #193) matters MORE under the corrected reading, not less: with removal-by-reply rare, each one carries more weight, and the detector was reading roughly 6% of the email on Microsoft and a 57-character snippet on Gmail.

findings_from_stage_1.what: Client offboarding is manual and untracked — a departing client's details are kept in a folder outside the system, 1-2 times a month.
findings_from_stage_1.why: Prospect personal data belonging to a departed client, held outside any retention or deletion path. A data-lifecycle gap the product does not know exists.

findings_from_stage_1.what: Nobody knows how often mailboxes disconnect, or who notices.
findings_from_stage_1.why: Google OAuth is in Testing mode, so drops are expected roughly weekly. An unmeasured failure on the sending path is the same class as the unreadable bounce rate.

access_level_basis: CORRECTED from "onsite" by cycle 47, and the correction matters more than it looks. `onsite` is the ONLY level in references/access-levels.md that requires zero compensating checks, so declaring it did not merely overstate the access - it switched the whole access-level rule off, which is why compensating_checks_done sat empty and passed. The claim was not true: all seven entries in answer_provenance record drafted_by "claude", sourced from prisma/schema.prisma, src/server/**, the git log and .bidlow/STATE.md. Nobody at BidlowAI has watched anybody at OpensDoors do their work. The real access is documents, the running system, and occasional direct answers from Greg - which is `async`. The skill's own words: an honest `async` run with its compensations is safer than an `onsite` claim you did not earn.

compensating_checks_basis.artefacts_received: Met, and unusually strongly, because this is the `rescue` route: the artefact is the running production system itself - the full codebase, the live screens walked on 2026-08-22/23/26, 44 migrations of schema history, the GitHub Actions run logs, .bidlow/STATE.md and CUSTOMER-READY-REPORT.md. That is the messy folder, not a blank form.
compensating_checks_basis.five_cases_reconstructed: Met on 2026-08-27 when the fifth case (the eight dead mailboxes) was traced; four had been traced before. The second half of this check - send the reconstruction back and ask "where is this wrong?" - has demonstrably fired at least once: Greg corrected the removal-request frequency in his own words on 2026-08-24, which downgraded finding F-01 from HIGH to LOW. See answer_provenance.frequency.correction_note.
compensating_checks_basis.written_premortem: Met in substance rather than in form. No document titled premortem exists, but exception_register E-01 to E-07 is the same exercise done against real incidents instead of imagined ones - each is a way the system DID fail, with a disposition. On the rescue route the postmortem is available and is strictly better evidence than a premortem.
compensating_checks_basis.riskiest_exception_first: Met, and inverted by the route. On a greenfield async build this means build the riskiest exception before the happy path. Here the happy path already shipped and was live, and the engagement has spent its cycles on exceptions ahead of features: the quarantine link misalignment, do-not-contact subdomain matching, the mock-provider send fallback, the two dead suppression sheets, the eight dead mailboxes, the 0% bounce rate. No new feature was built ahead of those.

compensating_checks_outstanding.why: The exception register was built from incidents found in the repository and the session record - it is BidlowAI's side of the story. OpensDoors' side has never been asked for as a structured checklist: a client complaint, a prospect who reacted badly, a list that turned out wrong, and what they did by hand to recover. Four of the prose answers end with an "ASK IN THE MEETING" list that is exactly this, unsent. It cannot be closed from inside a repository - it needs a checklist to go to a person and come back.

Fixed-price the first phase and change-control the rest, and say why. This is a commercial decision about a client relationship and about money, so it is not the agent's to record as done. See open_questions OQ-05.

entities.name: Client (a customer workspace)
states: Soft-deleted (deletedAt stamped, hidden from every normal path)
entities.dies: Super-admin soft-deletes, then a separate explicit hard purge. That purge is the ONLY deletion event in the system, and everything below dies with it by database cascade.

entities.name: Contact (a prospect)
entities.dies: Cascade on client purge. [stated] Greg, on a contact who moves company: the record is REMOVED, not re-pointed. [stated] Retention rule: prospect details are kept until they stop working, not to a fixed calendar period.
entities.source: prisma/schema.prisma plus Greg's stated data-model answers

entities.name: OutboundEmail (every email sent, body snapshot included)
entities.dies: Cascade on client purge only. No retention period, no scheduled cleanup.

entities.name: InboundReply and InboundMailboxMessage (replies and raw synced mail, full body text)
states: Claimed by a staff member (advisory, 30 minutes)
entities.source: prisma/schema.prisma; claiming added by PR #231, merged 2026-08-27

entities.name: ClientEmailSequence and its enrollments
entities.dies: Archiving STOPS it sending but deletes nothing. Real deletion is cascade on client purge only.

entities.name: ClientMailboxIdentity (a connected mailbox and its OAuth tokens)
states: Warming up (5/day, +5 every 5 days by mailbox age)
entities.dies: Cascade on client purge. How often a mailbox disconnects, and who notices, is recorded as UNKNOWN rather than as zero.

entities.name: ContactUniverse (the cross-client prospect warehouse)
entities.dies: IT DOES NOT. It has no clientId, so purging a workspace does not remove it: a prospect's name, email, phone and LinkedIn survive the deletion of the only client that ever knew them. Named as a gap, not as a design.

entities.name: SuppressedEmail and SuppressedDomain (a person who asked never to be contacted)
entities.dies: IT SHOULD NOT, and mostly does not - bounce and unsubscribe suppressions are append-only. But sheet-sourced suppression is REPLACE-ON-SYNC, so removing a row from the client's sheet makes that address sendable again. [stated] Greg: blocklists are CLIENT SPECIFIC, not shared across clients.
entities.source: src/server/email/bounce-suppression.ts plus Greg's stated data-model answer

exception_register.situation: Every outreach email carried an unsubscribe link on opensdoors.bidlow.co.uk while the From: address was the customer's own domain. That mismatch is the textbook phishing signal and it got mail quarantined. NOT an authentication failure - SPF, DKIM and DMARC were passing throughout.
exception_register.status: fixed 2026-08-22 on feat/zero-dns-send-profile; the app-domain fallback was removed entirely so it cannot return by accident

exception_register.situation: Do-not-contact missed subdomains: suppressing bt.com did not stop a send to someone@newsletter.bt.com, because the lookup was an exact match.
exception_register.status: fixed 2026-08-22; matching now walks up the domain's parents on label boundaries, so notbt.com and bt.com.evil.net still correctly do NOT match

exception_register.situation: A prospect row with no connected mailbox would have fallen through to a mock provider that returns success - an email recorded as sent that never existed.
exception_register.status: fixed 2026-08-09; prospect-send-transport-guard.ts now refuses the branch outright rather than gating it behind a flag

exception_register.situation: Staff isolation was asserted by a test, then found absent: any active staff member can open every workspace. Run for the first time on 2026-08-22, the test failed.
exception_register.status: the behaviour is the intended agency model, not a defect - but nobody had written that down, so a test spent nine days asserting the opposite. Now recorded in not_handling item 1

exception_register.situation: The product contradicts itself about its own sends: a client's Overview reads 'Activity - not started' while that same client's Activity tab reads 'EMAILS SENT 1'. Two different sources of truth.
exception_register.status: reproduced 2026-08-23; fix in PR #281 'fix(overview): the Overview said Activity - not started about a client that had sent', opened 2026-08-27

exception_register.situation: One mailbox connected to two workspaces duplicates raw inbound mail, body text included. Replies do not cross; the raw store does.
exception_register.status: found 2026-08-23, NOT FIXED. Open, and named as a customer-ready blocker in GRADES.json

exception_register.situation: The reported bounce rate read 0% across 1,209 sends with detection switched on. Traced 2026-08-27: the metric reads OutboundEmail.status == BOUNCED, which only the Resend webhook ever writes, while all outreach goes out through Microsoft Graph or Gmail. The number was structurally pinned at zero - the safety half worked (a hard-bounced address was still suppressed) while the measured half could never move.
exception_register.status: fixed and merged 2026-08-27, commit b358dcd 'fix(bounce): the reported bounce rate could never leave 0%'; verification recorded in efba021

not_handling.instead: Every active staff member sees every client workspace. This is the agency model: OpensDoors does outreach FOR its customers, so staff seeing every workspace is the product's design. ClientMembership already exists, inert, as the mechanism if it ever reverses. Selling one shared instance to two agencies who must not see each other is a REBUILD, not a feature.

not_handling.what: Delivery webhooks / a measured delivery rate
not_handling.instead: Because sending goes through the client's own mailbox rather than a bulk ESP, no provider reports delivery. 'Delivered' is shown as 'Not tracked' rather than guessed. Bounces come only from NDR/DSN bounce-backs arriving in the mailbox.

not_handling.what: Inferring related company domains from the domain string
not_handling.instead: bt.com does not imply bteurope.com and never can be derived from text. Related companies are detected from a SHARED MICROSOFT 365 TENANT and surfaced for the client to confirm (PR #244 gave the detection a caller and a screen; PR #273 added tenant matching). The client confirms; the system never guesses.

not_handling.what: A separate sending subdomain and a tracking domain
not_handling.instead: Sending is from the client's existing mailbox on their ROOT domain - that is what makes the zero-DNS architecture work. The accepted trade is that the client's ordinary business domain carries the reputation risk. Open tracking is switched OFF by default in production.

not_handling.what: Telling a limited company apart from a sole trader at import
not_handling.instead: UK PECR turns on the recipient's legal structure, and the import pipeline cannot distinguish them, so that question cannot be answered per recipient today. Named in DOMAIN-BRIEF-cold-email.md as a genuine, billable product gap rather than hidden.

not_handling.what: Automatic retention and erasure on a calendar
not_handling.instead: [stated] Greg's rule: prospect details are kept until they stop working, not to a fixed period. There is no scheduled cleanup and no erasure-on-request path in code, and that gap is recorded rather than assumed away.

not_handling.what: An automatic stop on a campaign that is bouncing
not_handling.instead: No send path reads the bounce rate, so a bad list is stopped by a person noticing. The compensating controls are a hard per-mailbox daily cap and the warm-up ramp. Now that the bounce number is real (E-07, fixed 2026-08-27) an automatic stop becomes possible and is a decision, not a gap.
